subject: Question about constrained GRMs and GRSMs

messages.author: 7f697e53a2e63a0e
messages.subject: Question about constrained GRMs and GRSMs
parts:
Hi Phil and everyone,

It feels like only the GPCM ("divide-by-total") family has a version constrained to items only varying in discrimination ("1PLish") with the Rasch Rating Scale.

Does it make sense / or is there any reason not to apply similar constraints in the "Graded" family?  For example, to use nested model comparisons to test if items vary in location (equal-slopes GRSM) vs. location + discrimination (GRSM) vs. location+discrimination+category structure (GRM).

It seems like it's very possible with mirt to do it (thanks for this!) from the item type "grsm", for example (for 6 items) : 
mirt(data, item = "grsm", model = "G = 1-6 \n CONSTRAIN = (1-6, a1)" ) 

But since I hardly see it in the literature I guess I'm wondering if it's a big mistake to do it (or if it's just for historical reasons that it's rare).

Cheers,
Nils

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Question about constrained GRMs and GRSMs
parts:
Hi Nils,

You certainly could apply those types of constraints and have similar benefits. From the statistical end, you improve the sampling variability of the model, so you typically get smaller SEs and other inferences when in fact all slopes are equal. I'm not sure if one obtains the so-called "objective measurement" properties Rasch-models often boast, but I imagine the total score statistics again become a sufficient source of information for estimating these models (don't hold me to that; I'm not sure if there's a proof of that anywhere). 

In any event, I wouldn't consider doing such a thing invalid when the model fit does not get worse. But then, that's my same philosophy when it comes to the Rasch family as well (I'm one of those measurement people who don't hold Rasch models in god-like regard, particularly because they rarely fit the data well). HTH.

Phil

Hi Phil, 

I have a more basic question related to constraining my slope parameter for my GRM. I am trying to constrain the slope parameter and then conduct a model test.
I have put together code from the help file, but it wouldn't run for me (most likely due to a mistake I'm making somewhere...).

Here is what I have so far:
grm2 <- mirt(data=dat.exp.num, model=1, itemtype='graded', CONSTRAIN=(Dis1-Dis18, a1))
The error I receive is ==> Error: unexpected ',' in "grm2 <- mirt(data=dat.exp.num, model=1, itemtype='graded', CONSTRAIN=(Dis1-Dis18,"

It's an 18 item scale and the items are labeled Dis1, Dis2, ... , Dis18.

Thank you so much for your help!!

Dan

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Question about constrained GRMs and GRSMs
parts:
The CONSTRAIN argument has to accept valid R objects; it does not try to parse any syntax. If you want to use the syntax mode consider using the string definition documented in the mirt.model() function; otherwise, you'll have to provide numeric item locations to make the current input work correctly. I'd probably just go with the syntax input since it's fairly intuitive. HTH.

Phil
